The question asks for the conditional probability that a student is in Year 10, given that they prefer to travel by bus. This can be represented as \(P(\text{Year 10} | \text{Bus})\). Using the formula for conditional probability, \(P(A|B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}\). The number of students in Year 10 who prefer the bus is given as \(x\) in the table. The total number of students who prefer the bus is also given in the 'Total' column for 'Bus', which is 160.

Therefore, the probability that a randomly chosen student is in Year 10, given they prefer to travel by bus, is the number of Year 10 students who prefer the bus divided by the total number of students who prefer the bus.

This is \(\frac{\text{Number of Year 10 students who prefer bus}}{\text{Total number of students who prefer bus}} = \frac{x}{160}\).
